Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 0. Absolutive (S and O) is zero-marked in Gurung. Table 4 (p.74) and Fig.14 (p.77) show Intransitive Subject: UM (unmarked) and Transitive Object: UM (unmarked). Glover describes the system as "nominative-ergative" (p.71), meaning A is ergative-marked and S/O are zero. Case table (p.70): Ergative=-d, with no absolutive suffix listed. Source: Glover 1974:70-74.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. 1sg pronoun Qa/Ia- takes ergative -d in transitive clauses: "Qa-d ... ax-ca-syo" (me-ER not-eat-EM, p.82 ex.42); "Ia-dl ... bo-la" (me-ER take-PLUP, p.77 ex.24). Source: Glover 1974:82,77.

curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. 2sg pronoun kxl takes ergative -d in transitive and imperative contexts: "kxl-d ax-bl-le tl-Ql-d" (you-ER ... stay-IM, p.85 ex.49); also kxl-d in ex.85 p.85. Source: Glover 1974:85,30.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs in perfective/past tenses. Ex.24 (p.77): "Ia-dl ... bo-la" (me-ER take-PLUP); ex.43 (p.83): "a99a-d cha'b thaudi-f" (office-ER stamp affix-PA). Source: Glover 1974:77,82-83.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs consistently in past tenses. Multiple examples with past (-l, -i) and pluperfect (-la): ex.24 "Ia-dl bo-la" (me-ER take-PLUP, p.77); ex.43 "a99a-d thaudi-f" (office-ER affix-PA, p.83). Source: Glover 1974:77-83.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs in non-past tenses. Ex.26 (p.77-78): "Ixy6-d ka'gada Ixyo-m" (we.INCL-ER paper look.at-NP); ex.27 (p.78): "bomw~-d puja la-m" (Brahmin-ER do-NP). Both use nonpast suffix -m with ergative-marked agent. Source: Glover 1974:77-78.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative -d appears in non-indicative (imperative) forms. Ex.49 (p.85): "kxl-d ax-bl-le tl-Ql-d" (you-ER [without-saying-anything] stay-IM) uses the imperative suffix -d with ergative-marked 2sg. The ergative is a CASE marker applied to the transitive/causative subject regardless of mood. Source: Glover 1974:85.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking is a case property of transitive subjects, not conditioned by realis/irrealis status. Glover's categorical statement (p.76): "ergative for the Transitive Clause." Ex.29 (p.122): "l~ma-d ... ax-cxu-m~la" (lama-ER not-prepare-PLUP.HAB) shows ergative with habituative -mala (modal/irrealis-adjacent). The unreal -mala (apodosis of hypotheticals, ex.27) has OCR-ambiguous text but no exception stated in the grammar. Source: Glover 1974:74,77,122.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Non-agentive A (Instrument, Non-instigative Cause) takes ergative -d. Table 4 (p.74) lists Transitive Subject roles as "A, C, AX" where C = Non-instigative Cause; all take ER marking. Ex.25 (p.77-78): "n~'-d ... p~'-l" (rain-ER soak-PA) — rain is Non-instigative Cause; book p.30 states Instrumental is "realized identically with -d". Source: Glover 1974:30,74,77-78.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Non-topical agents take ergative. The vast majority of ergative-marked agents in the corpus carry no topic particle: ex.25 "n~'-d" (rain-ER), ex.43 "a99a-d" (office-ER), ex.27 "bomw~-d" (Brahmin-ER), all without topic marking. Crucially, in ex.51-52 (pp.84-85), agents take BOTH ergative AND topic marker simultaneously (-d-am = ER+TOPIC), confirming ergative is not replaced by topic-marking. Source: Glover 1974:82-85.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Inanimate agents take ergative -d. Ex.25 (p.77-78): "n~'-d ... p~'-l" (rain-ER soak-PA); ex.43 (p.83): "a99a-d cha'b thaudi-f" (office-ER stamp affix-PA). Both are inanimate Non-instigative Causes/Agents with ergative marking. Source: Glover 1974:77-78,83.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative is a case-marking property not restricted to main clauses. Glover (p.71) describes -d as a "postposition" (case clitic) in the Relator system, applied to the subject of Transitive Clauses (Table 4, p.74). No restriction to main clause distribution is stated. Subordinate clause examples (gerund -ba, relative -bae) typically show deleted/implicit agents (contextually recoverable); no exception to ergative marking is noted for non-main clauses. Source: Glover 1974:71-74.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 0. Ergative alignment is not conditioned by any additional factor beyond transitivity. Glover's categorical description: "ergative for the Transitive Clause" (p.76), "unmarked for the Loc-Intransitive" (p.76). The ergative suffix -d applies consistently to all transitive subjects (Agent, Instrument/Cause, Agent-Experiencer) across tenses, aspects, and moods. No split conditioning (tense, person, animacy, topicality) is described. Source: Glover 1974:70-78.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 0. Ergative suffix -d is distinct from the genitive -e (possessive/genitive). Case table (p.70) lists: Ergative=-d, Genitive=-e (or -a/-'(a)). These are formally distinct markers. Source: Glover 1974:70.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Original value ? resolved to 0. Ergative suffix -d is distinct from the comitative -ne/-na. Case table (p.70) lists: Ergative=-d, Comitative=-ne/-na as separate case markers. Source: Glover 1974:70.
